name: movements-055
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: March or jog in place. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Low-impact cardiovascular exercise that simulates running without moving, ideal for warming up, improving endurance, or training in small spaces.

Row 1 column 2: Marching High Knees. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: A low-impact cardio and mobility exercise that strengthens the hip flexors and improves balance. 1. ​Movement: Stand tall and lift one knee toward your chest as high as comfortable. 1. ​Arms: Swing the opposite arm forward as you lift your knee, similar to a walking motion. 1. ​Core: Keep your abs engaged to maintain an upright posture. 1. ​Pace: Perform the movement with control, alternating legs rhythmically.

Row 1 column 3: Meadows Row. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: The Meadows row is a unilateral row performed with a landmine setup, overhand grip, and staggered stance. Lean your torso forward and grip the barbell. Rest the other forearm on the forward leg. Start this movement by driving the elbow behind you while retracting the shoulder-blade. Keep the working shoulder down. Pull toward your back hip until the elbow is level with your torso.

Row 1 column 4: Medicine ball booklet crunch. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Using a medicine ball as an overload will make the exercise heavier.

Row 2 column 1: Medicine Ball Chest Pass. Equipment: Medicine ball. Exercise guide: You will need a partner for this exercise. Lacking one, this movement can be performed against a wall. Begin facing your partner holding the medicine ball at your torso with both hands. Pull the ball to your chest, and reverse the motion by extending through the elbows. For sports applications, you can take a step as you throw. Your partner should catch the ball, and throw it back to you. Receive the throw with both hands at chest height.

Row 2 column 2: Medicine Ball Full Twist. Equipment: Medicine ball. Exercise guide: For this exercise you will need a medicine ball and a partner. Stand back to back with your partner, spaced 2-3 feet apart. This will be your starting position. Hold the ball in front of the trunk. Open the hips and turn the shoulders at the same time as your partner. For full rotation, you and your partner should twist in the same direction, i.e. counter-clockwise. Pass the ball to your partner, and both of you can now twist in the opposite direction to repeat the procedure.

Row 2 column 3: Medicine Ball Scoop Throw. Equipment: Medicine ball. Exercise guide: Assume a semisquat stance with a medicine ball in your hands. Your arms should hang so the ball is near your feet. Begin by thrusting the hips forward as you extend through the legs, jumping up. As you do, swing your arms up and over your head, keeping them extended, releasing the ball at the peak of your movement. The goal is to throw the ball the greatest distance behind you.

Row 2 column 4: Medicine ball twist. Equipment: Exercise ball. Exercise guide: In a seated position, the torso is rotated from side to side without forcing, approaching the knees and making the ball touch the ground from time to time

Row 3 column 1: Meditación guiada o libre. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Ejercicio mental de atención plena (mindfulness) que ayuda a reducir ansiedad, mejorar el enfoque y el bienestar general.

Row 3 column 2: Middle Back Shrug. Equipment: Dumbbell. Exercise guide: Lie facedown on an incline bench while holding a dumbbell in each hand. Your arms should be fully extended hanging down and pointing towards the floor. The palms of your hands should be facing each other. This will be your starting position. As you exhale, squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold the contraction for a full second. Tip: This movement is just like the reverse action of a hug, or trying to perform rear laterals as if you had no arms. As you inhale go back to the starting position. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 3 column 3: Middle Back Stretch. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Stand so your feet are shoulder width apart and your hands are on your hips. Twist at your waist until you feel a stretch. Hold for 10 to 15 seconds, then twist to the other side.

Row 3 column 4: Military Press mit SZ-Bar. Equipment: EZ bar. Exercise guide: On an SZ-bar grip your hands on the outside of each bend and stand with your arms straight down, palms facing your legs. Pull the bar (bending your arms at the elbow) to your chest, and the push the bar above your head (arms as straight as possible). Return the bar to your chest by dropping your arms at the elbows. Return the bar to it's origional position (stand with your arms straight down, palms facing your legs.)
